lines: Chord generator: builds a chord from a root note and a chord type, and puts it out as four separate 1V/oct pitches and as one polyphonic 1V/oct signal
Sets the root note of the chord over a range of -4V to 4V, rounded to the nearest semitone, with 0V giving C4
Sets the root note of the chord in place of the Root knob while a cable is patched, read as 1V/oct and rounded to the nearest semitone
Chooses the chord from major, minor, dominant 7, minor 7, major 7, sus2, sus4, diminished and augmented, one per volt from -4V for major to 4V for augmented
Chooses the chord type in place of the Type knob while a cable is patched, one type per volt and clamped to -4V to 4V
Sets the inversion from 0 for root position to 3; on a three-note chord 3 gives the same voicing as 2
Sets the inversion in place of the Inversion knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-3V
Spreads the chord: 0 leaves it as built, 1 drops the root an octave, 2 drops the root and the fifth, 3 drops the root and raises the third, 4 drops the root and the seventh on a four-note chord
Sets the voicing in place of the Voicing knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-4V
The lowest note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The second note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The third note of the chord as 1V/oct, after inversion and voicing have been applied
The fourth note of the chord as 1V/oct on a seventh chord; on a three-note chord it carries the lowest note raised an octave
The whole chord as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal, three or four channels according to the chord type, lowest note first; the extra octave that output 4 adds to a three-note chord is not included
Scale generator: builds a seven-note modal scale from a root and a mode, puts it out as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal, and quantises four separate pitches to it
Sets the root note of the scale over a range of -4V to 4V, rounded to the nearest semitone, with 0V giving C4
Sets the root note of the scale in place of the Root knob while a cable is patched, read as 1V/oct and rounded to the nearest semitone
Chooses the mode: major at -4V, then Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, minor and Locrian at 2V, and anything above 2V gives Locrian although the knob turns to 4V
Chooses the mode in place of the Mode knob while a cable is patched, one mode per volt from -4V, with everything above 2V giving Locrian
A monophonic pitch to be rounded to the nearest note of the current scale; the quantised pitch appears at the Out jack paired with it, and nothing is quantised unless that output is patched too
Carries the pitch at the In jack paired with it, rounded to the nearest note of the current scale; it stays at 0V unless both that input and this output are patched
The seven notes of the current scale as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal, one note per channel, starting at the root
ScaleCV.notes: The maker's README gives the Mode input range as -4V to 4V, but the code clamps the mode voltage to a maximum of 2V, so the top third of the knob and of the CV range all give Locrian.

lines: Builds a chord on a chosen degree of a scale fed to it, and puts the chord out as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal
The scale the chords are built from, as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal with one note per channel; with nothing patched the module uses C major
Transposes the chord an octave per volt over a range of -4V to 4V, rounded to whole octaves, with 0V placing the chord around C4
Transposes the chord in place of the Octave knob while a cable is patched, an octave per volt rounded to whole octaves
Chooses which degree of the scale the chord is built on, from the first at 0 to the seventh at 6
Chooses the scale degree in place of the Chord knob while a cable is patched, one degree per volt clamped to 0-6V
Chooses how many notes are stacked in thirds: a triad at 0, a seventh chord at 1, a ninth chord at 2
Chooses the chord type in place of the Type knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-2V, although the maker's README gives the range as 0-3V
Sets the inversion from 0 for root position to 4, and any setting above one less than the number of notes in the chord gives the topmost inversion
Sets the inversion in place of the Inversion knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-4V
Spreads the chord: 0 leaves it as built, 1 drops the lowest note an octave, 2 drops the lowest and third notes, 3 drops the lowest and raises the second, 4 drops the lowest and the fourth note
Sets the voicing in place of the Voicing knob while a cable is patched, clamped to 0-4V
The chord as a polyphonic 1V/oct signal, three to five channels according to the chord type, lowest note first
DiatonicCV.notes: The README gives the Type input range as 0V to 3V; the code clamps it to 0-2V and only three chord lengths exist.

lines: Picks a random note each time it is triggered and holds that note at its output as a 1V/oct pitch
A polyphonic 1V/oct signal giving the notes the random pick is drawn from; with nothing patched the pick is any semitone from C3 upwards within the span set by Range
Picks a new note on each press
A rising edge picks a new note; it reads high at 1V and low at 0.1V
Sets how often the lowest note of the polyphonic input is picked instead of a random one, none at -4V rising to every time at 4V, and it changes nothing while Poly In is unpatched
Sets the root bias in place of the Root Bias knob while a cable is patched, none at -4V rising to every time at 4V
Sets the span the random note is picked from, one octave at -4V rising to nine octaves at 4V
Sets the span in place of the Range knob while a cable is patched, one octave at -4V rising to nine octaves at 4V
The note last picked, held as a 1V/oct pitch until the next trigger
